title: fix(cli): drain run-dev.js stderr before oclif exits on top of the unbuilt-workspace diagnostic
body:
Fixes #13683

## Both hypotheses the card carries are falsified. The real mechanism is confirmed and reproduced.

### (1) "a formatter that cannot load because of the very condition it exists to explain" — FALSIFIED

- **The diagnostic path does not import `format.ts`.** `announceUnbuiltWorkspace` imports exactly `scripts/cli-unbuilt-workspace-lead.mjs` (whose only import is `scripts/cli-build-prerequisite.mjs`) and `src/utils/invocation.ts` (whose only imports are `node:` builtins). `invocation.ts`'s docstring says so deliberately: *"Pulling `./format.js` for CLI_NAME would drag chalk, zod and `@objectstack/spec` into a shim whose whole job is to print one line."*
- **Decisive: oclif's own error line went missing too.** The queue reds on `Error: command i18n:extract:nope.ts not found` in the same run. `handle()` prints that, not our formatter, and no import failure can delete it.

The card read `imported from packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts` as the diagnostic's own dependency. It names the **importer** — `format.ts` is what pulls `@objectstack/spec` inside a failing *command* module, i.e. the diagnostic's input.

### (2) "the fixture mutates shared `node_modules`" — FALSIFIED

`test/fixtures/unbuilt-spec-dist.hook.mjs` is a `registerHooks` **resolve** hook importing `node:module`, `node:path`, `node:url` and touching no disk. The `__unbuilt-simulation__` path is a specifier handed to node, deliberately non-existent — nothing is renamed. Its docstring already gives the reason: *"a test that renamed `packages/spec/dist` for a few seconds would break every other run in the box."* Fixture and test entered together in `e6fd1caf7b` (2026-08-29) and were unmodified at the failure, so this is the file that failed.

## The confirmed mechanism

`settings.debug` puts ~138 KB of oclif `ModuleLoadError` blocks on stderr **ahead** of the lead lines. A pipe holds 64 KiB. `handle()` ends in `process.exit()`, which drops undrained writes. A parent that is not draining gets one buffer and loses the lead lines **and** oclif's own error — measured 64721 bytes, both gone. Byte offsets say why only these: the lead line sits at 99.41% of the stream, the fix line at 99.65%, oclif's error at 99.70%; the surviving `[MODULE_NOT_FOUND] Warning` is at byte 11.

This is the **#6531 defect on stderr instead of stdout** — the one `src/utils/format.ts` documents for `emitJson`: *"the fix belongs at the write, not at the exit."* It is queue-only because a terminal is a TTY, written synchronously.

## ⚠️ The first version of this PR introduced a hang. It is fixed here, and it was not pre-existing.

Awaiting the write is only safe if something bounds the wait, and the first version's bound never armed:

```js
if (process.stderr.write(text, () => resolve())) return;   // early return
setTimeout(resolve, 10_000).unref();                       // never reached
```

`write()` returns `true` when the internal buffer is below the **highWaterMark** — not when the bytes have reached the pipe. Traced: `write() returned true, writableLength=7621`, so the early return fired and the cap was never set. The wait was therefore **unbounded**, not 10 s.

Measured against a reader that holds the pipe open and never drains — **base exits promptly, so this was introduced by this PR, not pre-existing**:

| scenario | base | first version | this version |
|---|---|---|---|
| reader never drains, pipe open | **1722 / 1710 ms**, exit 2 | **HANG** — alive at 25 s, 30 s ×2, 60 s; SIGKILL | bounded, exits 2 |
| read end destroyed at once | 1532 ms | 932 ms | 1383 ms |
| reader dies mid-flight | 1475 ms | 957 ms | 3009 ms |
| reader exits first (pipeline) | 1588 ms | 1602 / 1899 ms | prompt |

`EPIPE` does reach the write callback, which is why every closed-end path stays fast.

## The bound: no-progress, not a deadline

A deadline cannot tell a reader that is merely **slow** from one that is **absent**, and those want opposite answers. Progress separates them exactly. `STDERR_DRAIN_STALL_MS = 15_000`, derived — the derivation is in the code comment so it can be re-checked instead of bumped:

- A live reader under real load never stalled beyond **61 ms** (two samples of a vitest worker's event loop while this package's e2e suite ran beside it: 12 680 and 9 663 samples of a 10 ms timer; p999 = 24/25 ms, max = 61/57 ms). 15 s is ~245x that, so a slow reader is never cut off.
- The stall that actually loses these bytes must span the CLI's **whole run** — the bulk is emitted during `Config.load()`, the diagnostic ~3 s later, and bytes are lost only if the child exits while the reader is away. Measured child runtime: **1.0 s idle, 6.9 s contended**. 15 s is ~2.2x the worst.

Exceeding the bound degrades to the prompt-but-lossy behaviour this file had before the drain existed — **never to a hang**.

The bound firing, traced under a reader that blocks its loop for the whole run:

```
6884ms  write() returned false writableLength=75052
21932ms BOUND TRIPPED after 15048ms with pending=75052
```

## Verification

**Two ablations, direction stated before running, on `525b2dbd0a`.** Mutation proven on disk each time (blob hash equality plus anchor counts); restore proven by hash equality with the HEAD blob, empty `git diff HEAD`, clean `git status --porcelain`; trap in the same shell as the measurement.

- **vs base** (no drain) — predicted the case-4 truncation assertions red: `3 failed | 7 passed`, `expected 64721 to be greater than 65536` plus the queue's own two assertion strings, differing from the job log only in pid.
- **vs the first version** (early return) — predicted the mirror case red: `1 failed | 9 passed`, `AssertionError: expected 'SIGKILL' to be null`.

⚠️ **Two earlier test designs were discarded because they were measured to prove nothing**, and both are recorded in the file so they are not re-attempted:

1. Holding the pipe with `child.stderr.pause()` lets node fill its own 64 KiB buffer; ~128 KiB of headroom swallowed the run and the case passed against unfixed code.
2. A 4 s stall stopped discriminating once a contended box pushed child runtime past it — caught because the ablation against base came back **green**. A slow *continuous* reader failed the other way: it drains the bulk long before the tail is written, so the tail meets an empty pipe.

There is deliberately **no** assertion that the child waited for the bound: whether bytes are still pending at the tail moves with load, so that assertion would red on one run and pass on another. The suite pins the property that holds either way — the process ends — and the bound's firing is shown by the trace above.

**Gates**, all on `525b2dbd0a` after merging `origin/main` (the pre-merge derivation warned STALE TREE and was discarded): **named 34, ran 34, unreconciled 0**, both `comm` directions empty. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 0 and `check:type-check-debt` exit 0 (*"28 ledger entries re-measured, 1468 raw tsc errors total, none above its recorded number"*) after building the closure; one gate, `check-test-completeness.mjs`, needs a test-run log CI tees and is NOT MEASURED locally by its own statement. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` exit 0. `check-nul-bytes` exit 0.

⚠️ `packages/cli`'s `tsconfig.json` has `include: ["src"]` and `tsc --listFiles` shows **0** `test/` files in that program, so package typecheck says nothing about the edited test file and cannot move the debt ledger. Checked separately against the package's own compilerOptions: exit 0, 0 errors, no `as any`.

## Not established, and left that way

Whether this is **new** remains unestablished — not established on a quiet commit, and main's runs in that window are unusable as a control.
